note: Tax-expenditure estimates = federal income-tax revenue the Treasury forgoes because of the credit, holding taxpayer behavior fixed. NOT the same as credits states allocate or cash spending. JCT publishes rolling 5-year windows; each pamphlet is a fresh forecast under a new baseline and law, so figures for the same year differ across pamphlets. Combined = individuals + corporations. Values in billions of dollars.

jct_current.climb_note: The steep FY2025->2029 rise reflects the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's permanent 12% state-ceiling increase and lowered bond-financing threshold for buildings placed in service after Dec 31, 2025 (JCX-45-25 p.19). Not an organic trend.

treasury.source: U.S. Treasury, Office of Tax Analysis, Tax Expenditures (FY2026)
treasury.note: Both JCT and Treasury attribute nearly all of the credit to corporations (the banks and companies that buy the credits); the individual share is tiny. Totals agree closely (FY2026: JCT ~15.0 vs Treasury 15.17).
